correctness.rationale: The binary-digit recurrence r_(2n)=r_n and r_(2n+1)=r_n xor (n mod 2) yields a uniform four-letter morphism a->ab,b->ac,c->db,d->dc, with 0 on a,b and 1 on c,d. For fixed binary alphabet, greedy shortest factors covering both letters (arches) count the maximum length of universally available scattered target subsequences. The complete three-initial-state, four-letter weighted transfer table has m=4 base and composes exactly for all higher m, with <=1 error from (5/16)2^m per aligned block and independent entering state. Every interval has at most two maximal aligned dyadic blocks per scale, giving 2(floor(log2 N)+1) error; the a-transfer gives dyadic parity term. A fresh independent transducer verified m=0..11 and all 11,830 selected factors, and direct digit coding checked; finite checks corroborate induction only.
residual_risks: Bound is not claimed asymptotically optimal and fixed alphabet is essential; no general automatic sequence theorem asserted.
Finite checks do not establish uniform all-factor asymptotics; table induction and dyadic decomposition do.
